title: Tokenization — Build a Useful Vocabulary
key_insight: Subword methods begin with small pieces and learn common combinations. Frequent text becomes compact while unfamiliar words can still be assembled.
body:
## Build a Useful Vocabulary

Whole words make rare names impossible, while single characters make every sentence very long. A practical tokenizer balances those extremes.

Subword methods begin with small pieces and learn common combinations. Frequent text becomes compact while unfamiliar words can still be assembled.

Special tokens mark boundaries or roles. Their exact meanings belong to the model and tokenizer pair, so mismatching versions corrupts inputs.
common_mistakes: A tokenizer directly verifies every factual answer.
Every token is always one complete English word.
Token numbers have the same meaning across all models.
mini_exercise: Draw “Build a Useful Vocabulary” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Every language-model input and output passes through a tokenizer, so its choices affect meaning, length, and cost.
explain_back_prompt: Using “Build a Useful Vocabulary,” explain Tokenization without assuming the listener knows modern AI.
